title: No division by zero
text: Dividing both sides by $$x^2$$ would quietly remove the case $$x=0$$. Since $$x=0$$ satisfies the equation, that step would lose a valid solution and therefore isn’t allowed.

title: Square roots lose a sign
text: Taking a square root at this stage either loses solutions or forces us to split into several separate cases. Writing $$\pm x^2=\pm x$$ really creates four equations to solve. That’s inefficient and invites mistakes. There’s a cleaner route.

title: Why not plug in values?
text: While checking values like $$0$$ and $$\pm 1$$ may suggest the solutions here, testing values can never confirm that no other solutions exist. Factoring and applying the zero-product property yields a complete and reliable argument.

title: Subtracting $$x^2$$ from both sides
text: When we subtract $$x^2$$ from both sides, we can factor an apply the zero product property. Done carefully, this method guarantees that all solutions are found and none are lost.
